{{Short description|Genus of flowering plants}} {{Automatic taxobox |image = Funchal, Monte - Choisya ternata (Orangenblume) IMG 1974.JPG |image_caption = ''Choisya ternata'' |taxon = Choisya |authority = [[Carl Sigismund Kunth|Kunth]]{{cite web |url=http://www.ars-grin.gov/cgi-bin/npgs/html/genus.pl?2518 |title=Genus: ''Choisya'' Kunth |work=Germplasm Resources Information Network |publisher=United States Department of Agriculture |date=2008-03-21 |accessdate=2009-09-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007171439/http://www.ars-grin.gov/cgi-bin/npgs/html/genus.pl?2518 |archive-date=2012-10-07 |url-status=dead }} |synonyms = ''Astrophyllum'' [[John Torrey|Torr.]] & [[Asa Gray|A.Gray]] |synonyms_ref = |subdivision_ranks = Species |subdivision = [[#Species|See text]] }} [[File:Choisya ternata closeup.jpg|thumb|]] '''''Choisya''''' {{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|ɔɪ|z|i|ə}}''Sunset Western Garden Book,'' 1995:606–607
But {{IPAc-en|ˈ|tʃ|ɔɪ|z|i|ə}} or {{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|w|ɑː|z|i|ə}} per the OED: {{OED|Choisya}} is a small [[genus]] of aromatic [[evergreen]] [[shrub]]s in the [[rue]] family, [[Rutaceae]]. Members of the genus are commonly known as '''Mexican orange''' due to the similarity of their flowers to those of the closely related [[Orange (fruit)|orange]], both in shape and scent. They are [[native plant|native]] to southern North America, from Arizona, New Mexico, Texas and south through most of Mexico. In its generic name [[Friedrich Wilhelm Heinrich Alexander von Humboldt|Humboldt]] and [[Aimé Jacques Alexandre Bonpland|Bonpland]] honoured Swiss botanist [[Jacques Denys Choisy|Jacques Denis Choisy]] (1799–1859).{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NJ6PyhVuecwC |title=The Names of Plants |first=D. |last=Gledhill |edition=4 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-86645-3 |year=2008 |page=105}} ==Description== The species grow to {{convert|1|-|3|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall. The [[Leaf|leaves]] are opposite, leathery, glossy, [[Leaf shape|palmately]] compound with 3-13 leaflets, each leaflet {{convert|3|-|8|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|0.5|-|3.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} broad. ''C. ternata'' has three broad leaflets, while ''C. dumosa'' has up to 13 very narrow leaflets. The [[flower]]s are star-shaped, {{convert|3|-|5|cm|in|abbr=on}} diameter, with 4-7 white [[petal]]s, 8-15 [[stamen]]s and a green [[carpel|stigma]]; they are produced throughout the late spring and summer. The [[fruit]] is a leathery two to six sectioned [[capsule (fruit)|capsule]].{{Cite journal |first=Cornelius H |last=Muller |date=1940 |title=A Revision of Choisya |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2420869 |journal=The American Midland Naturalist |volume=24 |issue=3 |pages=729–742 |doi=10.2307/2420869 |jstor=2420869 |issn=0003-0031|url-access=subscription }} ==Uses== [[File:Choisya 'Aztec Pearl' detail.JPG|thumb|175px|''Choisya'' 'Aztec Pearl']] ''Choisya'' species are popular [[ornamental plant]]s in areas with mild winters, grown primarily for their abundant and fragrant flowers. The foliage is also aromatic, smelling of [[rue]] when bruised or cut. The flowers are also valued for [[Forage (honey bee)|honeybee forage]], producing abundant [[nectar]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2024}} The following [[cultivar]]s have gained the [[Royal
